stories.title: Man arrested in Widdecombe murder investigation
stories.summary: Police in the UK have arrested a 26-year-old man on suspicion of murder in connection with the death of former Conservative minister Ann Widdecombe. Devon and Cornwall Police said officers were called to an address in Haytor at 11.40am yesterday and found Ms Widdecombe dead, having sustained serious injuries. Devon and Cornwall Police Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman told a press conference that Ms Widdecombe's death was not being treated as a terrorist incident and that police have no reason to believe it was politically-motivated.. "Detectives from the force major crime investigation team have launched a murder investigation, and are conducting extensive inquiries into the circumstances surrounding Ms Widdecombe’s death," he said.

stories.title: At least 12 dead, 23 unaccounted for after Spain wildfire
stories.summary: At least 12 people have died and 23 others are unaccounted for following a deadly wildfire in the southern Spanish region of ‌Andalusia, according to officials. One Spaniard was among the victims and the rest appeared to be foreign nationals. The area is a popular holiday destination and home to many European expats. The blaze ⁠near ‌Almeria is Spain's deadliest ⁠wildfire in more than two decades.

stories.title: Cyclist, 40s, dies after Co Kildare hit-and-run incident
stories.summary: A cyclist in his 40s has died after a hit-and-run incident in Co Kildare. Gardaí believe that the incident, on the R445, Dublin Road, took place between 10.30pm last night and 12.30pm this afternoon. The man was pronounced dead at the scene and his body has since been removed to Naas General Hospital, where a post mortem examination will take place in due course. Gardaí are appealing to anyone who may have been travelling on the R445 between Kildare Town and the roundabout at Junction 12 of the M7 between those times to come forward.

stories.title: Garda acquitted of raping wife, guilty of child cruelty
stories.summary: A garda has been acquitted of raping his former wife but convicted of child cruelty against two of his children. The 48-year-old man had pleaded not guilty to all the charges. After deliberating for more than nine hours, the jury this afternoon found him not guilty of two counts of raping his former wife, but guilty of all four charges of cruelty to his two daughters. He was convicted of two counts of child cruelty and one count of assault causing harm to his now 24-year-old daughter and one count of child cruelty against his now 17-year-old daughter.

stories.title: Long dry spell brings early start to harvest for farmers
stories.summary: Harvest time for tillage farmers has been creeping in earlier in recent years, with many grain growers already well into harvesting their first crop of the season due to the warm weather. It is happening as a high temperature warning takes effect for 12 counties for the coming days. One of the counties included is Laois, where tillage farmer Clive Carter has just started harvesting his winter barley crop. "We've had a good run of weather, so it's great to get going at it," he said.

stories.title: £10m British govt payout over IRA double agents
stories.summary: The British government has provisionally agreed to pay £10 million to the families of those abducted, murdered or interrogated by its double agents in the IRA. Principal among them was west Belfast man Freddie Scappaticci, known as Stakeknife, who operated in the IRA's internal security unit, hunting suspected informers. At the same time, he was passing information to British Army intelligence and other branches of the security forces. A Belfast law firm KRW Law acts for 19 families whose loved ones were murdered by the IRA.
